Update July 2015, This TV has started acting up, I will be calling the 1-800-samsung and see what they say but with looking at the information on the web, it seems as if this tv is experiencing the same problems that their older TV's had which is power supply issues. It won't turn on sometimes, or it will take 30 seconds to power up, or other variations. I wish that I had known about these issues before I purchased this TV because I might have looked at different manufacturers..

Called the 800 number found out that manufacturer warranty is gone obviously. No offers of a free diagnostic or anything like that. They did provide a local number for technition but with it being a weekend chances are no one is there. I am going to see if there is anything I can visually pick up in the power supply and do some basic testing. (I did work as a power sports tech for a number of years and was a pretty serious computer hobbyist as well) after that will have to see. Will do another update after this is resolved one way or another

text_fidelity_a:
CORSAIR Hydro Series H105 AIO Liquid CPU Cooler, 240mm Thick Radiator, Dual 120mm PWM Fans I've wanted to try one of these liquid CPU coolers for ages, but it always been a little too cheap to spend the extra money on one, and I confess I've been mildly concerned about using a liquid anything inside my computer. I'm glad I tried this out.

This particular model has a radiator style grate which the fan sits on (there is some conductive paste included), then has tubes leading to the cooler unit. The water is totally enclosed in the system, and I can see no danger of leakage. The fan is quiet and unobtrusive.

It has a four pin connector, so if your computer has a four pin connector as well, your computer can control the speed of the fan. However, the four pin connector can also connect to a three pin connector and it works fine, you just lose that extra bit of control.

The one small improvement I'd like to see is that the water/cooling area only goes to one side of the radiator type grate, not around all of the edges, so one side of it will always be hotter than the other. It still disperses heat well, just seems like a less efficient system then it could be.

Lastly, I love the thumbscrews included for installing. I hate dealing with normal screws, and the thumbscrews are such a thoughtful touch that it made me think well of the company for including them.

Overall, if you've been on the fence about testing out one of these new liquid CPU coolers, I don't see any reason not to try out this one. The price is reasonable for what it is, and it looks like a highly effective setup, certainly better than just using a fan.
text_fidelity_b: CORSAIR Hydro Series H105 AIO Liquid CPU Cooler, 240mm Thick Radiator, Dual 120mm PWM Fans

text_fidelity_a:
Bose SoundTrue Headphones Around-Ear Style, Black Bose is primarily known for their active noise canceling (ANC) phones though they have for years offered non-ANC phones. This is my first pair of Bose phones that are not in the ANC class of headphones and my impression of them is mostly positive. I do see some room for improvement, though.

First off, these are without question the lightest headphones (aside from ear buds) that I have ever worn. I am a bit odd in that I actually prefer heavier headphones but this is strictly a preference, not a criticism. In spite of the weight, the phones fit very nicely and do not feel like they're about to slip off if you lean down. This is not to say they're tight, but they are tight enough to hold well. They're easy to adjust too, so getting them to fit just right is simple enough. If exceptionally lightweight headphones are your thing, this is what you want.

The cord is a little different than other phones I have used in that the jacks on either end are of different sizes. This is good and bad. It's good in that there's no question of how to attach the cord because it only fits one way. But, it also means that a normal cord that comes with practically any other headphone will not work.

The sound quality is definitely better than average but not perfect (certainly not audiophile-level). The sound spectrum seems to be fairly well balanced. The highs are good and the "edges" are crisp and clean for most tracks. The midrange is ok but slightly hollow. The bass is very good without being overdriven. One of the problems with a lot of headphones is that they tend to overdrive the bass which is fine if you really like your bass, but too much can overpower the rest of the spectrum and give some of us headaches. That these phones do not over-amplify the bass is a pleasant surprise.

Having a pair of Bose QC-15 ANC phones, I can compare the two models' sound profiles and there are some slight differences. Where the QC-15s are great at the highs and overdrive the bass, the midrange is sorely lacking. The SoundTrue get the bass right and have good highs but fall slightly short on the midrange (though still better than the QC-15s). Comparing just the sound profiles and ignoring the ANC function, I prefer the SoundTrue over the QC-15s.

The carrying case is nice and should provide some protection when packed for travel. I would have preferred a slightly harder and more crush-resistant case but that's me being picky. There's not a lot of extra room in the case so storage is not really an option with the case.

The price is a little high ($180 as I write this) and that might be a little steep for some. It comes down to whether a less expensive set of phones delivers the same (or better) sound profile.

My overall impression of the Bose SoundTrue headphones is positive. These are very comfortable and exceptionally lightweight and the sound quality is good though not perfect. These phones are above average and are worth consideration if you want non-ANC headphones or if you're looking for very lightweight headphones.
text_fidelity_b: Bose SoundTrue Headphones Around-Ear Style, Black

Pre-release technology reviewers commenting on the price of the Kindle Oasis are wrong. The new Kindle Oasis is worth the the price Amazon is charging, including cover it hardly represents at all an increase in price when compared with a Kindle Voyage with cover. Yet it provides the two most asked for improvements in mobile devices: increased battery life reducing the need to frequently recharge, and improved screen legibility (new sans-serif Ember font, and more LEDS that provide increased brightness).

“When we are immersed into the story of our favorite books, only that world matters.”

Pre-release technology reviewers have compared the Kindle as a single purpose e-reader, to multipurpose devices like in smartphones, tablets and computers. When we choose to read, we are seeking a bit of solitude in the day and night. Oh, how easy it is to remember being annoyed with yet another incoming phone call, text message or email. The power of focus!

“The tactile feel of a book”

Pre-release technology reviewer have labelled the Kindle as luxurious with it’s leather cover. How soon we forget our books covered with leather! And we are willing to pay an extra price for it!

As I sit across the street from the one and only Amazon retail store “in the world”, I have unboxed and set up my new Kindle Oasis. Maybe I am one of the few ordinary people outside of Amazon and the technology press in the world to have been able to purchase one so soon. The feeling reminds me of going to a release party in the same shopping center for the latest Harry Potter novel.

This Kindle is new, like the latest release from our favorite author.

It connects me to reading anywhere, late at night when there is little light.

The Kindle Oasis is magical.

text_fidelity_a:
DEWALT DXFRS800 2 Watt Heavy Duty Walkie Talkies - Waterproof, Shock Resistant, Long Range & Rechargeable Two-Way Radio with VOX My husband has a lot of use for communication on jobs he has to do in the contracting world. We have had some jobs here at the house which required walkie talkie communication. Let's see how these performed.

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
HOW ARE THEY BUILT?
These walkie talkies are tough. They come with the batteries outside of the units, so you have to put them in.

HOW TO PUT BATTERIES IN
You will need a very pointed screwdriver or a small Phillips head screw driver to get the battery cover off. When you screw it back in, it is pretty sturdy.

HOW TO TURN IT ON
The on button on the top is large and easy to cold, dirty, or gloved hands to turn on and off. You can also adjust volume.

CASE?
The case snaps on and off of the units. They stay hooked to the clothes pretty well as long as you are not moving around a lot. In that case, we found them most useful to hold the walkies in the pockets with the clip.

CLARITY OF SOUND?
The clarity of sound was superb. We were doing roof work on the top of a third story and they worked great. We also had to do work about 100 ft away from the point of origin of a wiring job, so we needed that for communication to test the connections. Again, they worked great. Very clear and worked very well.

TOUGH?
These have been dropped a few times and worked very well.

RECHARGING?
The recharging unit has a place for both walkies to be charged. The plug is separate from the base that you charge in. Each receptacle has a red light on it to let you know that the walkie is charging. The plug is small so you can use it on a power strip or in the wall outlet without blocking other outlets. Recharging is fast- within the hour- and they seem to last quite a while before needing to be recharged.

CLIPS
The clips have to be removed prior to charging.

CHANNELS
The different channels we used all worked well. We did not have to use them in a very busy area with multiple walkies, however, so we did not get to test it with a lot of walkie talkie traffic happening on a huge job site.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For a very sturdy set of walkie talkies which charge up quickly and last a long time, these are fantastic for contract work and any jobs that we have had to do. My husband plans to take them to his jobs as well when needed. They have a decent range to them and are easy to operate even with gloves on.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. We really love these walkie-talkies. They have been fantastic so far for all of the jobs we have had to use them for. I will update if we have anything valuable to add in the future as we continue to use them over time.
text_fidelity_b: DEWALT DXFRS800 2 Watt Heavy Duty Walkie Talkies - Waterproof, Shock Resistant, Long Range & Rechargeable Two-Way Radio with VOX

text_fidelity_a:
Joby Gorillamobile Ori for iPad (GM12-01AM) Multipositional Protective Lightweight Aluminum Case Silver UPDATE: This also works very well with an HP Touchpad. It's slighly smaller than the ipad so the fit is not as tight, but still quite stable. If you position the Touchpad correctly the on/off button works fine, and the volume button sort of works (can lower the volume easily but raising it requires a bit more effort).

Original review:
This is probably the most useful accessory I've every used for the iPad. Truly amazing in how it can be folded and unfolded to provide ease of use regardless of how you're using the iPad.

All the options make for a bit of a learning curve, however. I tried to follow the diagrams in the user's guide, but didn't really "get" how to use this until I watched the manufacturer's video. Highly recommend that as a guide to how to get the most out of this stand.

I'm especially pleased with being able to use it as a stand for viewing a movie (the position they call "Popcorn and a Movie" in the manual). Excellent when more than one person want to view the screen.

I can't comment with any degree of certainty as to it's longevity since I've only been using it for a few days, but it seems very sturdy. I'll update the review should that assumption prove faulty.

My big question is whether it will fit the iPad 2. Clearly it will cause problems with the cameras, but it is such a tight fit with the iPad 1 (which is a good thing in a case for security) that I'm hopeful that it will work with the iPad 2 with (perhaps) a bit of padding to make up for the thinner profile. I'll update with my experiences with the iPad 2 later this month once I have one in hand.

But regardless of fitting other models, this is an outstanding accessory for the iPad 1. Highly recommend.
text_fidelity_b: Joby Gorillamobile Ori for iPad (GM12-01AM) Multipositional Protective Lightweight Aluminum Case Silver

text_fidelity_a:
Clip-Case Universal Ergonomic Tablet Stand (Tripod Kit) and Smartphone Mount for iPhone iPad iPod Galaxy Droid Kindle Nook This is one of those "why didn't I think of it?" type products. At first glance, it seems quite simple - basically a mini tripod with attachments that allow you to mount a tablet or phone. But after working with it for a while, it's clear a lot of thought went into this.

The tripod is well made and sturdy, consisting mainly of metal. The ball joint at the top is controlled by a built-in key that allows you to loosen and tighten it so it stays put. Each leg extends independently, so you can set the tripod so it is tilted upward (for example, to position a tablet so you can watch a movie at your desk). The attachment screw base has a rubber non-slip insert to protect whatever you're attaching against scratches. It includes a lanyard, but you can easily remove it (which I did) if it's not needed.

The tripod is very compact -- folds up to about 4.5 inches long and about 1 inch wide, so it's easy to carry. With the legs fully extended it is just under 9 inches tall. The legs have a thick rubber tip that keep it well balanced and positioned. I was a bit concerned that the legs didn't have locks, but the tension of the pull out extensions was more than adequate to keep the legs extended even when it was loaded down with an 8.9 inch Kindle Fire.

Impressive quality given the price - much better than expected.

You can also use the tripod as a camera tripod since the attachment screw is a standard size. It worked fine with my Panasonic and Canon point and shoots.

But the star of the show is the clip. You attach it to the back of the device case (you could attach it to the device itself, but it's not recommended) using an adhesive pad. The pad is removable, but is not reusable, so you want to give some thought before you stick it to the case. Once attached, it fits into a "smart mount" that, in turn, attaches to the tripod. Sounds kind of complicated, but it's very simple to use. There is an included instruction sheet, but you can pretty much puzzle it out by just looking at it.

The clip and smart mount are plastic, but seem more than sturdy enough for the job. They clip together with an interlocking system that kept my Kindle very solidly positioned while I was using it.

The only negative I see is the adhesive pad. As with any adhesive, you need to clean the point of contact very well (an alcohol pad is included in the box) and let the adhesive cure for 30 min. I think it's a safe bet that some people won't do both those steps, which opens the door to a significant point of failure.

But, provided you read the instructions, this is a very nicely designed and useful product. Highly recommend.
[The manufacturer provided the product for review]
text_fidelity_b: Clip-Case Universal Ergonomic Tablet Stand (Tripod Kit) and Smartphone Mount for iPhone iPad iPod Galaxy Droid Kindle Nook

text_fidelity_a:
Toshiba TY-CWU700 Vintage Style Retro Look Micro Component Wireless Bluetooth Audio Streaming & CD Player Wood Speaker System + Remote, USB Port for MP3 Playback, FM Stereo Digital Tuner, AUX Input This unit is large and not at all like the dimensions listed on Amazon. It is 5 inches high (top to bottom), 8 inches deep (front to back), and 16 inches in long (side-to-side).

WHAT COMES IN THE BOX:
- one speaker unit with both left and right speakers inside the large housing
- one power cord
- one FM antenna cord / wire
- one AAA battery
- one remote
- three user guides; one in English, Spanish, and French (I love this because I can keep the instructions in English and throw out the others)
- one limited 1-year warranty insert

FEATURES:
- Bluetooth speaker
- CD player
- FM Radio with ability for 30 preset radio stations
- Ability to operate controls via remote or front of the unit buttons
- Clock
- Sleep / timer function up to 120 minutes in 15-minute increments
- LED Dimmer
- USB terminal that supports USB memory (thumb drive) in FAT 16 or FAT 32 format
- Line In port to plug in an external audio device such as earphones / headphones

The sound this produces when I play my CDs was awesome and music to my ears. I also paired this speaker with my Google Nexus 7 Tablet (2013 version Android device) and my iPad Pro 12.9 and experienced moderately powerful sound there as well. The FM radio was staticky but that was due to the location of where I placed my unit. When I did receive a station, the sound was great.

In summary, this produces beautiful sound. As a Bluetooth speaker, it does not produce as powerful a sound as my [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Block Rocker]] but it is still good. The addition of the FM radio is a nice touch. I also like that it functions as an LED clock. The instructions and operation of the unit take a bit of getting use to and can be confusing but I was eventually able to figure it out; although I may have to consult the pamphlet every now and then. Overall, this is a well-rounded unit for indoor use but the unit is larger than I expected. It is as large as those old AM/FM amplifiers from years ago and has a retro 70’s look (see attached picture).

PS For those who are interested in comparisons, this is my sixth Bluetooth speaker. I ordered five other Bluetooth speakers over a several year period. I have a [[ASIN:B007ZG03DG Bose Wave Bluetooth Music Adapter]], which is not very good and a [[ASIN:B00MPMK3GW Goal Zero 94014 Rock Out 2 Green Solar Rechargeable Speaker]] which does not work when paired with some devices and, when it does pair well, it usually lacks the powerful sound I am looking for.

I also purchased one [[ASIN:B00SNBCBBY ION Audio Block Rocker (iPA76A) | Portable Bluetooth Speaker]] and one [[ASIN:B01N17AQ7U ION Audio IPA88 Tailgater Flash Wireless/Bluetooth Speaker]] both from Costco. I absolutely love the Block Rocker (except for when paired with my iPad Pro) and I only like the Tailgate Flash. The lights on the Tailgate Flash annoy me because they have to be turned off every time I power on the unit. Nevertheless, the sound from the ION speakers are usually awesome. The IONs are the only ones I use frequently indoors (even though they are more of an outdoor Bluetooth speaker). They are battery powered powerful speakers and the sound is intense. If one wants Bluetooth only with the capability of travelling with them without having to find a power outlet, then these are worth considering.

I also have a [[ASIN:B01MUG5WIN Sony XB20 Portable Wireless Speaker with Bluetooth, Blue (2017 model)]] which pairs well with my HP Omen Laptop and moderately well with my Nexus 7 and iPad Pro. However, this has to be charged first just like the Goal Zero speaker that I dislike.

PS My boyfriend connected his iPad 3 to this one's Bluetooth and loves it for listening to Podcasts. In order to get the volume as loud as he wanted, he also used the volume controls on the side of his iPad in conjunction with the volume knob on the Toshiba. On another note, he mentioned that the controls located below the CD player are very small for someone who has eye problems and I would agree with that. What I find inconvenient is that the button to open and close the CD player is there so that when the CD is open, I have to put my hand underneath it to close if I am not using the remote. Nevertheless, he loves this Toshiba just like I do.
text_fidelity_b: Toshiba TY-CWU700 Vintage Style Retro Look Micro Component Wireless Bluetooth Audio Streaming & CD Player Wood Speaker System + Remote, USB Port for MP3 Playback, FM Stereo Digital Tuner, AUX Input

Rii I8 Mini 2.4Ghz Wireless Touchpad Keyboard With Mouse For Pc, Pad, Xbox 360, Ps3, Google Android Tv Box, Htpc, Iptv (Black) When my review sample arrived I tested it on a few devices and it worked perfectly on each. The first device was my ancient ThinkPad T61 running Windows XP. I inserted the dongle (look in the battery compartment for it), and it was immediately recognized and activated. As soon as I turned on power to the keyboard I was able to navigate using the touchpad, bring up an editor and type.

The next tests were with my [[ASIN:B00JA5DCNS Keedox® Quad Core RK3188 Android 4.2 1080P 5G 2.4G HDMI Bluetooth 4.0 Smart TV BOX]], then using a [[ASIN:B00C7SK2J2 Micro USB OTG Host Cable to USB 2.0]] I connected the dongle to my Galaxy Note 3 phone and Tab 3 10.1 tablet respectively and was texting and performing other functions. This is truly a plug-and-play keyboard/touchpad.

One final thing I love is the battery is a standard BT51 that can be purchased just about anywhere if you are such a power user that you need a spare.

It's set up for thumb style texting, so most folks will be immediately comfortable with it. I love the tactile feedback from the keys, which were a pleasure to type with, as well as the array of function keys and buttons. If you spend a lot of time on smaller devices this is a dream come true. At about thirteen bucks at the time of this review it's a bargain for folks who are heavy texters.

text_fidelity_a:
RHA MA750 (Discontinued by Manufacturer) I dislike reviews where the comments just gush about the product. But I have no other choice but to do just that - these are some incredibly good earphones!

I've been using RHA earphones for a couple of years and have been impressed by the sound quality given the price. I own several earphones, but the ones I reach for most often by far are my RHA MA350s even though they are one of the least pricey pair of buds I own. Great sound quality and excellent build quality.

Well, the MA350s will be spending some time on the shelf. The MA750s are a clear step up. (Gush alert:) These are simply amazing! They can handle anything I thrown at them so far, with great bass that doesn't boom or bottom out, clear midrange and sharp upper range. Just fantastic performance.

I was a bit concerned about the ear wrap design since I usually find that type of design to be irritating for long-term use, and especially irritating when wearing them while exercising. But no problems at all even with extended wearing. Very comfortable and no chafing even when running.

The MA750s come with an extensive set of replacement ear cushions in a variety of designs. I can't imagine that a person would not be able to adjust these to fit perfectly given there are 10 different potential configurations. The cord is stout but flexible, with significant reenforcements at the plug end.

Even the packaging is upscale, with a high quality box with a front panel (with a magnetic enclosure) that opens to revel the earphones and tips nicely displayed. Very Apple-esque in their presentation.

Also included is a leather (or what feels like leather) carry case. The tips come with a metal holder that fits into the case so you can keep everything neatly stored and protected. A small point, but is shows that some real thought went into every aspect of this product.

While these are priced higher than other RHA earphones, the cost is well worth it. Even at the current price point, these outperform my Bose, Shure and Sennheiser earbuds that are priced far higher, and way outperform buds in their MA750 price range.

Huge recommendation for these - try as I might, I just can't find a single criticism to voice about them.
[Sample provided for review]
text_fidelity_b: RHA MA750 (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

To monitor, I plug my trusty MDRV6's into the monitor out of the 302 mixer, which is listening via its return to the headphone output of the Nikon. With a knob turn, I can then listen to any of the mixer's three inputs directly or to the camera's return confidence feed.

If it sounds good in the Sony MDRV6's, it'll sound good in the edit.

Yes, there are way more expensive headphones, but I know how the MDRV6's sound, I trust them, and they never break.

text_fidelity_a:
Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black For moderate priced earbuds, these are pretty good. The sound quality is much better than average, with smooth response across the range. The highs are detailed, and not shrill. The midbass is clear, with no unnatural peak that sometimes passes for "bass boost". The deep bass is natural, and not artificially strong. Very easy to listen to for extended sessions.

For comfort, these are pretty average -- not the best comfort, but not bad either. There are interchangeable ear tips you can try out for the best fit. There's a lot of personal preference as to what's going to stay in the ear comfortably. The earbuds are angled, so you have to pay attention to the left/right orientation.

This is advertised as "iPhone compatible", meaning that there's a mic with tiny + and - buttons attached to the left ear piece. I'm a BlackBerry guy, and I'm happy to report that the mic works fine with my BlackBerry Bold 9700. But the + and - buttons don't have any effect (they don't raise or lower the volume). However, pressing the small button between the + and - buttons will either pause the song that's playing, or mute a phone call. Pretty handy.

Sound isolation is not a strong point of this set. I wasn't sure what to expect, so I guess I'm not disappointed. Probably you'd want to look elsewhere if sound isolation is important to you.

Durability may also be an issue. The wire is very thin, and it feels fragile, especially where it connects to the earbud. I'll know in 6 to 12 months whether these will stand up to regular use. The 90-degree plug will take wear better for many people, depending on how it connects to your phone, MP3 player or computer. Comes with a little storage pouch, which is good protection for the set when not in use.
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDREX38iP/BLK EX Earbud with iPod Remote Control - Black

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Aspire TC-885-UA91 Desktop, 9th Gen Intel Core i3-9100, 8GB DDR4, 512GB SSD, 8X DVD, 802.11AC Wifi, USB 3.1 Type C, Windows 10 Home,Black I have typically bought and loved Dell Inspiron desktop computers for use with school and business purposes and have been very satisfied over the years.

When we were told that we needed Windows 10, I tried to download it to my old Inspiron but was not successful because my Dell equipment was really too old for a successful install; I really love the Inspiron and Windows 7.

In February 2020, I bought a new desktop and had a really stressful experience. There was something wrong with the configuration, and the tech support people could not get the computer to perform properly. After many hours online with tech support, the situation started to seem hopeless. The pandemic began to become worrisome both here and in India (tech support), and I returned the desktop for a fully refund.

Last week I started again trying to find a desktop with Windows 10. I didn't want to spend a small fortune for a computer that I use primarily for shopping, email, browsing, and, rarely, online banking transactions. I found this Acer after reading good reviews. Since my current desktop is an I3 and has basically the same specs, I chose this computer rather than the I5.

One of my siblings told me that Acer has a long history of excellent quality and that I would be pleased. He was right! This desktop is great.

PROS:
Comes with Windows 10 pre-installed. Plug it in. It's ready to go.
Norton Security is pre-loaded with a 30-day trial period.
The computer is extremely user friendly. I had no struggles with glitches with any of the programs.
Bloatware is easy to recognize and easy to remove (a Windows 10 feature).

CONS:
There really are no cons except that the "feel" of the plastic components is not as hefty as some of the desktops that I have used in the past (other companies). The plastic casing of the tower, the keyboard, and the mouse are beautifully designed but not quite as heavy as prior desktops that I have owned. That isn't necessarily a "con," and I like the keyboard, mouse, and computer case. Very attractively designed.

MY RATING:
5 STARS

The price, the ease of use, the beautiful performance -- a great buy!
text_fidelity_b: Acer Aspire TC-885-UA91 Desktop, 9th Gen Intel Core i3-9100, 8GB DDR4, 512GB SSD, 8X DVD, 802.11AC Wifi, USB 3.1 Type C, Windows 10 Home,Black

Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th) I bought this to take on a trip. I am traveling very lightly, and I do not like waiting around. I have a smartphone, but it's getting harder for me to read on it. I have an iPad Air, but even that can be a little big on a cramped plane ride.

Plus, I sold my other seven inch tablets (a Galaxy and a MeMo), and I miss them. They're the perfect size for reading. This tablet is so much nicer than what I would have been willing to deal with for fifty bucks. However, there are a couple of issues that keep this from being a five star device, even at this price.

The first is that using an sd card to hold content is no easier than it is with the older tech media players I have spent a fair amount of time trying to figure out. If you can download it to your computer, you can put it on the card and then load the card into the Kindle, but the Kindle doesn't treat the card like a drive that you can save to. A firmware update could fix this.

The second is the weight. I'm actually not sure how I feel about this one. It's definitely heavier than I expected. But it feels solid. So, maybe I like it?

Everything else is great for what I am using it for. Reading books. Very light web browsing. Playing with my FireTV. Buying music to play on the Echo. In other words, it's a great tool for accessing the Amazonverse. As a regular tablet? Good for the price.
text_fidelity_b: Fire Tablet with Alexa, 7" Display, 16 GB, Blue - with Special Offers (Previous Generation - 5th)

text_fidelity_a: Sony MDRNC7/BLK Noise Canceling On-Ear headphones (Black) My husband and I bought two sets of these three years ago from Circuit City during their going out of business sale. We both travel quite a bit and were in need of decent headphones for longer flights (let's face it, the ear buds provided by the airlines just don't cut it). My husband accidentally left his set, in their pouch, in the seat back pocket on a flight last year and was in need of a replacement set for our trip to Germany last week. I was amazed by the price when I came onto Amazon to check - $29.99 was a steal compared to the $80 we spent a few years back! This headset is not the top of the line, but it is effective in canceling out the low aircraft drawl while in-flight. (They are also quite nice when you need to drown out the crying child in 23F. ;)) The battery life is remarkable. I have had to change the battery on my set only twice in the three years I've owned it. The only complaint that I have, which results in the four star rating instead of five, is that after wearing the set for a few hours (i.e., Amsterdam to Houston, TX), my ears begin to ache on the outside. It is almost like the headset becomes to tight over longer periods of time. I tend not to wear earrings on airplanes, so I can rule out the possibility of pinching. Other than that slight achy feeling, these are wonderful for the casual traveler and the price simply cannot be beat!
text_fidelity_b: Sony MDRNC7/BLK Noise Canceling On-Ear headphones (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th) July 27, 2018 - update. To preface, let me say that my previous Fire tablet was with me for just under 5 years, is still working fine except that it doesn't hold a charge as well as it used to (which is why I went with a new one). This tablet I've had since February so we're talking 5 MONTHS instead of years. As of today, the screen is cracked. Since I don't carry it with me the way I used to carry the previous one, and since the case I have this one in is sturdier than the previous case, and since, to the best of my knowledge, this hasn't been dropped, I'm not pleased. I'm thinking this probably arrived this way, since the crack can only be seen when it is a just the right angle to a bright light. Of course, it won't be covered under the "limited" (that should read VERY limited) warranty, and apparently, I failed to buy the protection plan because I was thinking this was as well built as my previous Kindle. Wrong on all counts. So I will say that it just went down to a 3 star review, partly for the company and not just the Kindle. For all the trouble I had with the books and being able to read books I'd purchased, this was the last thing I expected to happen. If I buy another reader, since I've already figured out I don't like Amazon knowing everything I do through Alexa, it won't be a Kindle.

February 2018 - I just received my new Fire 10 last week. I am moving from my old Fire 8.9, because the battery had decided not to keep a charge, and I was lucky to get 2 hours out of it at one time. Terrible for traveling or using it where there wasn't a plug in available.

I had an unholy amount of problems with the Kindle books on my Fire 10. First once all 1300 books were downloaded, an awful lot of them, at least 20% were unreadable, because of a DRM error. Kindle support did a fine job of straightening that out, although it cost me about 2 hours on chat before it was completed. Then, some books didn't download when they should have so it took what seemed like two days to get them all organized and downloaded. But finally that was straight.

My next problem was with Alexa, whose answer to me is normally, I'm sorry I don't understand. But if the television is on, she apparently can understand the Olympic announcers because she responds to them right away. Because she responds to other voices, once at a restaurant this week, I have to turn her off when we're in public. Obviously, she's far too friendly with strangers. I had heard that this would be a problem, just didn't think it was going to be mine.

I am not a technophile, I can only tell you as an average person using this Fire tablet for all sorts of activities during the day, that it is functional, quick, and works very well with the apps I have loaded. I use my Fire far more that I'll ever use my phone for reading, purchasing, browsing, so I'm very pleased with how it operates. I like the size of the screen, I like the weight. I did not buy Amazon's cover for it, which I'm finding might have been a mistake, but I'll deal with that after the tablet and I have bonded. I can honestly say that when my 8.9 new it didn't work this quickly, so color me pleased.
text_fidelity_b: Fire HD 10 Tablet with Alexa Hands-Free, 10.1" 1080p Full HD Display, 32 GB, Marine Blue (Previous Generation - 7th)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version) I knew right away that these would be my office headphones. I have a mechanical keyboard that I use at work, and the office I work in is semi-open. There's a *lot* of noise coming every-which-way. These are a much-needed accessory to my work productivity, as I'm easily distracted by things in my periphery, whether visually or auditory.

The presentation is great. The box is very high quality, reminiscent of the recent Samsung Galaxy device boxes. A smooth matte feel with gloss--weirdly pristine. The box slides out of the slipcover and you get the headphones already in the case. What I like is that they're folded, and there's even a little sheet underneath the phones that always reminds you how to put them back in. Also included is a 3.5mm cable in case you don't want to use Bluetooth, a charging cable, and an adapter. The case is nice, but as I keep mine at work I can't testify to its durability. There's a thin mesh net on the backside in case anyone needs to store one or two thin headphone accessory/-ies along. The accent colors are a nice light copper/rose gold color. I love that color; I'm glad it's getting more attention in recent years.

It didn't take long to charge the headphones, so they come with a little bit of juice. As soon as you turn them on, you get a soft beep along with a voice indicating they're turned on. Nice responsive feedback. Once I put them on I could hear the headphones working to drown out the sound; there was a thick veil of soundproofing that was draped over my ears as soon as the earpads touched them.

The first thing I did was listen to podcasts through the Pocket Casts app and .flac music through Poweramp v3. With podcasts, the difference was phenomenal. Listening to "Wait, wait... Don't tell me!" made me feel as though I were in the audience. The music was fantastic...until I tried on my other headphones which I use for music only.
I thought the bass might've been too strong with the Sony headphones, and I was right. After using even "cheaper" headphones like the Audio-Technica M50x, I could tell the Sony had too much bass. I'm not sure if that's partly because of the noise-canceling technology or what, but the bass can be toned down a bit, methinks.

I then proceeded to download the supplementary app to get the fullest suite of attributes the headphones can get. The app works well, and I didn't experience any hiccups while actually using the app. The only hiccup was when I was trying to download the update. It took *forever*. Almost an hour and it was just halfway through. I decided to bring them to work the next day and let the app sit there while updating. Thankfully, it remembers the progress, even though the app kept crashing during the update process.

There are some optimization tweaks in the app, some sound profiles to let you configure the noise cancelation level (yes, level; the noise cancelation is pure software; you can set it to drown out the most noise as possible or have no noise cancellation at all), and even a little snippet of what is currently playing through the headphones. A simple UI with all the features you need.

The first few days I used it I was active, and I kept noticing that my ears sometimes would pop depending on whether I sat down or arose quickly. Another weird thing is that when I take the headphones off, my ears sometimes need a minute or two to adjust. There's so much noise in the world! After taking the headphones off I can hear HVAC activity and my loud work neighbor who's otherwise not that loud.

I had some headphones with some touch controls before and always found them tacky. I used them once when I first got them and never again. But with these headphones, I'm always using the tap gesture to play/pause and the swipe gesture to raise or lower the volume. There are also swipe gestures to skip or go back a track, but since I never do that anyway I never use those gestures. You have to be careful with the tap; when it works, it works. But the whole surface isn't the active portion and you have to hit it right in the center. Sometimes I'm hitting my finger against my ears trying to find the spot and hurting myself in the process. I tested the gesture where you put your entire palm on the cup to turn off the noise canceling feature and let the mic allow incoming conversation, but not after the third try. I could hear the other people just fine, but I found the right hand over my ear felt awkward, and one person didn't realize I could even hear them. Putting your hand over your headphones isn't a gesture people immediately see as you paying attention to them.

The headphones are extremely lightweight and comfortable to use; I left them on for about two hours once before having to take them off. I actually was surprised with how light they were; when I got the Amazon box I didn't believe it was my headphones. It was much lighter than expected.

For my first noise-canceling headphones I'm pleased. The sound balance can be better (less bass), but they make for fantastic headphones to use at work. I wasn't sure what I was expecting with noise-canceling technology. I thought it would drown out all noises, but you still can hear the occasional mutter; it just won't be distinct.

Oh, forgot to mention the battery life. I charged it only once and have been using it for a week, at about an hour or two each day. Still going well. If you press the power button once it will tell you the battery level. AFter the initial update the voice indicator might give the wrong battery level (it did for me), but give it about ten or fifteen minutes to adjust and it will go back to normal.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version)

VANGUARD Endeavor ED 8x42 Binocular, ED Glass, Waterproof/Fogproof, Black (ENDEAVOR ED 8420) This is my third pair of binoculars. Years ago I purchased a pair of Yamaha bincolars for about $200 of a similar power (8 or 10) and diameter (42 or 50) for wildlife viewing. The lens stopped working after two years so I then purchased a fantastic pair of waterproof 10 x 42 Leica binoculars that have served me well on vacation and when I went on safari.

However, these Endeavor ED 8420 binoculars by Vanguard (at the current list price of $339.88) seem to be almost as good as my $1,000 Leica's with the exception that these are not waterproof and the power is only 8 instead of 10. According to the package, it also comes with a lifetime warranty.

The only trouble I had was putting on the carrying strap. The diopter ring was easily set and locks securely once set. The eye cups are easily adjustable. However, because I wear glasses, I had to leave them in the down position. The objective lens cap is fixed onto the binoculars with rubber rings and the eye cap (cover) is hooked onto the carrying strap. This means there are no pieces to lose, which is nice. The body cover has a nice grip to it so the bincoulars are unlikely to fall out of my hands. The weight is 25.8 ounces.

According to the instructions, there is also a tripod adapter which sits between the lens. I honestly don't know if this would work on all tripods after you screw off the cap because of its position and I did not try this feature. A carrying case and lens cloth also is provided.

Although I am not a bincoluar connoisseur by any means, this pair I received for review have impressed me. Time will tell if they last like the Leica's or fail like the Yamaha I had. However, if they fail there's always that lifetime warranty where all that has to be paid is shipping both ways. That's not too bad a deal.
text_fidelity_b: VANGUARD Endeavor ED 8x42 Binocular, ED Glass, Waterproof/Fogproof, Black (ENDEAVOR ED 8420)

text_fidelity_a:
Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer** I'm typing this review on this Chromebook right now! I'm a graduate student, and I got tired of my Windows computer installing updates every time I opened my laptop. It was frustrating. I just wanted to open my laptop and get right to writing my homework. Now I can! It's also very lightweight, so I can easily bring it and all my books with me to class. It holds a charge for at least 2-3 days of active homework use and general internet fun for me. It starts up almost instantly when I open it! The screen size is fine, and I often have two windows open at the same time, side by side. I've been trying to read more articles online without printing them, and using online textbooks via my Kindle app. After a bit of a learning curve, this has worked out awesome, because if I have my Chromebook, I have ALL my textbooks with me, plus my course information, and my notebook to write things down. I love it. Plus, it doesn't get hot or make a whirring sound when you use it for a long time. I like that because I often use mine while I"m sitting on the couch.

Getting used to using the Chromebook had some hiccups. First, I recommend using Google Docs for writing because it has an offline mode. The Windows OneDrive and cloud version of Word works ok, but if your internet has any interruption, you can't keep typing. That's annoying. So use Google Docs, and don't worry about it! (But if you're working on a project with someone, and they use Word on a Windows laptop, you can collaborate with them no problem using the cloud version of Word.) Second, organizing my files confused me, until I realized that "Save As" is now "Move to folder.' Also, you can download a few files to your Chromebook, so if you need to upload an attachment to Blackboard, you can pretty easily. You'll use your Google Drive for much of your file storage. I did connect my OneDrive to my Chromebook, but it's through a third party app thing, and the connection always has to be redone, so I don't really rely on that, and I plan to move my OneDrive stuff to my Google drive soon.

The only thing that was really hard was setting up my Chromebook to print to my WiFi printer. Google cloud print is in beta, and in theory, it's awesome. When you're done setting it up, you could print to your home printer from anywhere, using your mobile device. However, Google your printer and how to set up cloud print, and give yourself some time to set it up. If you're in a rush, you should just plug your printer into your Chromebook.

Lastly, since many public schools are going Chromebook, I thought it was a good idea to get one myself. I'm working on getting my Master of Arts in Teaching to be an elementary/middle school teacher. Using one for my own schoolwork helps me be able to help students use their Chromebooks. Additionally, the price is so nice, I don't worry about having to ever replace my Chromebook, because if it was damaged by schoolchildren, I'd only be out about $160 (instead of $2000 for a Mac). I'm even thinking of getting one for my mom, since most of what she does online could be done on a Chromebook, too.

Oh, and one very last thing, the keyboard is really enjoyable to type on. The keys are spaced comfortably, and the individual keys make a nice clicky sound, are springy, and are nice and thin, for fast typing. I know that might sound weird, but I'm picky about my keyboards.
text_fidelity_b: Acer Chromebook, 11.6-Inch, CB3-111-C670 (Intel Celeron, 2GB, 16GB SSD, White) **Discontinued by Manufacturer**

VIZIO M-Series All-in-One 2.1 Immersive Sound Bar with 6 High-Performance Speakers, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, Built in Subwoofers and Alexa Compatibility, M213ad-K8, 2023 Model I CHOSE this model over another because of the supposed built-in Alexa compatibility. You can indeed connect the soundbar to an Echo device *as a regular bluetooth connection*, but the instructions to enable Auto VA (auto virtual assistant mode) via Bluetooth so the soundbar maintains a BT connection with Echo while using other inputs DOESN'T WORK. The instructions say to first connect the soundbar to Echo via BT (✅), and then to press the Bluetooth button for 10 seconds to enable Auto VA (❌). HOWEVER; after five seconds, the soundbar enters Bluetooth pairing mode. I've tried dozens of times, connecting and disconnecting the BT connection with Echo and restarting and resetting the soundbar: NO DICE.

It's frustrating because this feature is in the title of the product and is clearly described in the User Manual — and yet it doesn't work at all.

I imagine Auto VA via AUX input works okay, but that means I have to move my Echo or get a wicked-long audio cable, neither of which I want to do.

However, otherwise the soundbar sounds fine. Not quite as good as the Bose Companion computer speakers I used previously, but whole worlds better than the built in TV speakers. It's just a shame that I have disconnect and reconnect to Alexa so often.
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO M-Series All-in-One 2.1 Immersive Sound Bar with 6 High-Performance Speakers, Dolby Atmos, DTS:X, Built in Subwoofers and Alexa Compatibility, M213ad-K8, 2023 Model

Audio-Technica ATH-LS50iSBK In-Ear Monitor Headphones with In-Line Mic & Control, Black As a disclaimer, I'm just an ordinary consumer (vs. a technical expert) when it comes to headphones, speakers, or earbuds. Having said that, here's my experience with these in-ear headphones:

As earbuds go, these are not as lightweight as the much cheaper, AmazonBasics and Panasonic ones I have owned. However, it's a weight difference that isn't really a problem, once I get them securely fastened around my ears.

The sound is wonderful. It has much more clarity than the inexpensive earbuds I usually buy. So to some extent the adage, "You get what you pay for," seems to apply here.

These earbuds have a useful extra: they have a microphone built in. Because of that, you can use it to speak on your cellphone, if you'd rather use this than a Bluetooth. Or if you are listening to entertainment media on your cell phone when you get a call, you won't have to unplug this earbud to take the call.

The microphone control has only one button, an on/off toggle switch. There are no volume adjustment buttons.

These earbuds seem to be well constructed. The cord is thicker and sturdier than my low-cost AmazonBasics and Panasonic earbuds.

The piece that fits into your ear has a relatively large casing compared to my other earbuds, but no doubt this is because the technology is more complicated.

These earbuds are an expensive buy for those of us who normally pay $7-12 for earbuds, but if you like to listen to music, it might be worth it.
text_fidelity_b: Audio-Technica ATH-LS50iSBK In-Ear Monitor Headphones with In-Line Mic & Control, Black

Unfortunately, my hair is thinning because I lose some each time I remove the headset.  Regardless, this bluetooth is extremely easy to synch with my Droid and it's recognized each and every time I turn on the Bluetooth in the car.  I wear this only for driving and I don't care that passersby give me funny looks, it works great.  The earpiece is larger than most contemporary bluetooth devices, but it's cushiony and comfortable for long drives.  The microphone is sensitive and responsive.  I haven't had a complaint yet with any call.  Slipping the earphone onto the headband is a simple task, and I find that I'm wearing it 90% of the time, preferring that to the ear wire and no band.  My main criticism other than the hair pulling of this design is that it takes some getting used to to operate the touch controls as well as turn the device on and off.  When off of the band, it's an easy feat, but no so when it's attached and you can't bend the microphone down completely. Because you have options for charging this set, you're a step ahead, and with an adjustable headband, it fits most head sizes.  It's a good set.

text_fidelity_a:
ARCTIC S111 USB-Powered Portable Stereo Speakers for Tablet/eReader/MP3/Computers, Balanced Treble/Superior Bass - Blue Note: I would love to love this speaker set, but it has inconsistent performance with various devices. I received a review sample and was pleased by the sound when I plugged this into the phone port on my ThinkPad T61. The sound was clear and I could hear every note on the album that I use to test speakers (Miles Davis' [[ASIN:B000002ADT Kind of Blue]]). I use that album because the instruments in the ensemble cover low, mid and high range frequencies. The bass was a little thin, but with the speakers less than two feet away the sound was rich and I was happy.

Where I started to experience problems was when I plugged this into the 3.5mm port on my Samsung Galaxy Note 3 phone. There was static in the mix. The same with my [[ASIN:B00D029NNA Samsung Galaxy Tab 3 10.1 inch]] - static interfered with the music. My final test was to plug the 3.5mm cable end into an [[ASIN:B00AEJJRBK Avantree Cara Bluetooth 4.0 Handsfree stereo Car Kit with mic]] and connect via bluetooth. The sound was crystal clear.

I am not sure what conclusions to draw. It could be something wrong with the Samsung phone and tablet, although both work perfectly with headphones which I have directly plugged into their 3.5mm ports. It may be that the 3.5mm cable and interface on the input of this speaker is overly sensitive to impedance and the slightest deviation will induce static. I am not sure, but because I was unable to get the same quality consistently across all devices with which I tested these speakers I subtracted two stars.

Construction is exceptional, although I wish the design employed removable USB and 3.5mm cables instead of the fixed ones that provide power and signal inputs, and connect the two units. As it stands if a cable breaks it will take some skill to repair it. With removable, off-the-shelf cables a broken one can be rectified with a trip to an electronics store.

Overall, on the two devices that I tested with which these speakers worked the sound was spectacular. On the other two it was unlistenable. If you are connecting this to a bluetooth receiver it's probably a safe choice, but if you are connecting this to anything else I would proceed with caution.
text_fidelity_b: ARCTIC S111 USB-Powered Portable Stereo Speakers for Tablet/eReader/MP3/Computers, Balanced Treble/Superior Bass - Blue

text_fidelity_a:
USB Power Strip Portable Travel Charger Outlets 2.1AMP 1AMP 21W 5Foot Power Supply Cord With Universal Plug Input From 100v-240v Power Sockets USB Charger Station 4 Port 5v 1A/2.1A USB Charger (White) This is a very unique and awesome product. It wasn't listed near the beginning of my Amazon search results, so it took me a while to find it. But it's AWESOME!!!

The first thing I do when I get to a hotel room or a cruise ship cabin is to set up my charging station. We have phones, iWatches, Kindle, iPad, and rechargable power packs, so we end up having a lot of potential things to charge. Setting up the charging area is a high priority. The best place is on a table or desk, so we can spread out our rat's nest of cables and devices with easy access. However, power outlets are often in inconvenient places, especially on a cruise ship. (On cruises, in the past I would actually bring a small extension cord.)

Anyway, this super clever travel charger solves the problem. I can plug it into the wall outlet, and run the cord up onto a table or desk. It's perfect.

Actually, the 4 USB ports isn't nearly enough for us, so one of these chargers wasn't going to entirely solve my problem. Theoretically, I could use two of them, but that's overkill in the sense that I don't need long two cords. Since this charger has a wall-plug type of outlet on the charger itself, I already have regular wall power at the charger on the table. I don't need to run a second cord from a wall outlet. Therefore, I use a small 4-port USB charger without the cord, and plug that into this charger. That gives me 8 USB ports up on the table for easy access. Here's the 4-port charger without a cord that I plug into this one:
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07JH9R89T/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_asin_title_o01_s00?ie=UTF8&psc=1

I have never seen a charger with a cord like this before, and I am very impressed with how clever and useful the design is! The one problem I found was with the child protection piece inside the slots on the charger's power socket. (This is the 110V power socket on the charger.) Because of the child protection piece, it can sometimes be very hard to get something plugged into that socket. The protection piece needs to slide to the side, so you can't just push the plug straight in, like you would at a wall socket. You need to put the prongs into the slots at an angle, and pry the protection piece out of the way. It's a pain. So, if you don't need the child protection, and you intend to use that socket, you'll probably want to remove the protection piece.

Here's how to do that. The top surface is a snap-off cover. Pull it up in the middle of one of the side, and slip a little screwdriver in there to carefully pry around and pop it off. Then there's a second cover inside that isn't attached, and will almost just fall out. On the back of that second cover, you'll see the two little springs and the plastic protection piece. Pull out the springs and the protection piece, and then put it all back together.

[NOTE: Do not remove the child protection if there will be children near it, or if you have any other safety concerns about its removal. Remove it at your own discretion and your own risk. I'm not telling you to remove it. I'm just telling you how to remove it if you want to.]

Anyway, I actually went a step further. The socket seems to be designed to accept any plug in the universe, so there are a lot of extra holes and spaces (i.e. it's not just two little slits for the normal US plug). I took white electrical tape, and taped over all the extra holes and spaces on the secondary (internal) cover, leaving just the two slits open. Then after popping on the outer cover, you just see the two open slits. All the other openings are covered internally with the white electrical tape. I think it looks much better, but this is purely a cosmetic step.

At first, it seemed like the clip for the plug is on the wrong side. It's on the same side as the USB ports. If you leave the plug in the clip (and leave the cord wrapped around the charger), then rotate the plug down 90 degrees, you can plug it into a wall outlet and the charger would be flush against the wall, hanging down from the wall socket. That seemed like it should be a nice neat way of using it without extending the cord, if desired. However, you can't do that because the USB ports end up against the wall, and you can't access them. If the clip was on the opposite side, it would work fine. As it currently is, in order to use it, you need to flip it around so the USB ports are facing out. But since the plug clip is on the wrong side, the charger sticks out from the wall at an angle. At first this seemed like a design flaw. Then I read in the instructions where it specifically says you shouldn't do any charging while the cord is wrapped around it. Presumably that's a heat issue. Therefore, it is probably designed this way on purpose, to discourage you from attempting to use the charger with the cord wrapped around it.

The bottom line is that there is no design flaw. It's prefect just the way it is. And you need to unwrap the cord when you use it, which is fine with me, since having the cord extended is the best feature of this charger.

Anyway, I think this is an awesome little gadget.
text_fidelity_b: USB Power Strip Portable Travel Charger Outlets 2.1AMP 1AMP 21W 5Foot Power Supply Cord With Universal Plug Input From 100v-240v Power Sockets USB Charger Station 4 Port 5v 1A/2.1A USB Charger (White)

text_fidelity_a:
Roku N1100 HD Media Player (Old Model) I've been researching ways to increase my cable channel happiness and reduce the costs. My research started a while ago, but a Cosumerist post about subscriber fees really got my goat. Look at all the junk channels that we are forced to pay for. I could care less about any sports channel or 90% of everything else. It is my opinion that we should be able to choose extra channels separately after we hook up with basic cable. You'll also notice that BH charges extra for a special HD tier. Sure it's only $6 a month, but geez, look how much markup there is. Anyways, you get the idea. I don't have any issues with BH. They've served me well for a few years. But I need more of what I want. Not what BH thinks I want.

So, I dropped down to basic cable and purchased a Roku HD unit. Set-up was a snap. I used HDMI for the TV and stream with a N router.

OMFG! This thing is amazing! In short, it streams unlimited Netflix offerings to your TV. The cheapest Netflix subscription ($9) is all you need. Plus it streams Amazon Video On Demand, and a bunch of internet channels. You can stream wirelessly or hard wire with an ethernet cable.

Can you tell I'm excited? Anytime I can boost my entertainment for less dollars is always a good day. The Roku will pay for itself in 2 months after switching to basic. And its HD!

Sigh...I must go.

I've been watching the original Dr. Who from the 60's.
text_fidelity_b: Roku N1100 HD Media Player (Old Model)

text_fidelity_a: YYK Bone Conduction Headphones On-Ear Earbuds Built-in Noise-Canceling Mic,IPX7 Waterproof Sports Wireless Earphones Bluetooth Headphones for Workout Running Red My husband works out and I recently (accidentally) washed his workout shorts with his earbuds in the pockets. Of course it was his fault for leaving them in there, but I felt some guilt, so when offered, I ordered these as a replacement. This review is based on his experiences: The Bone Conduction Sports Bluetooth headset was very comfortable (in the ear). Connecting it to a phone was very easy. It comes with everything you need: a manual, charging cable, and an extra set of earbud covers/caps for different ear sizes. You can control/adjust the volume and skip songs via a control (push button) on the earpiece. Even while running, they felt secure. And finally, his only hesitation in giving this product 5 stars is the ability to hear outside noise. He feels that this is a result of how the earbuds are designed. Unlike other headsets he has owned in the past, these sit “outside” of the ear canal/not directly in the ear, which means you do lose some sound quality. Perhaps, if these buds fit inside the ear a little deeper, or you use a headband to press the earbuds closer, the sound quality would improve. In conclusion, he believes these earbuds are not “bad,” especially at this price point ($50 on Amazon), but it could be improved. 4 stars

I didn’t even know they existed, but I’m glad they do -- I didn’t like it at all when Apple moved away from MagSafe.

I’ve been using the converter for a few weeks and usually leave the small connector bit -- the oval piece -- plugged into my laptop even when I’m not charging it. It’s small enough that I don’t notice it.

The magnetic connection is reasonably strong, though the magnets could be stronger. The other bit, the part that plug into the charging cord, doesn’t always “click” on the first attempt.

I’m able to plug in other USB C cables, but my USB C to USB 3.0 adapters don’t fit.

Aside from those quibbles, I like this converter quite a bit. I’m even tempted to get another for the backup charger I have in my upstairs office, because I like having the safety and convenience of MagSafe so much.

TIANSHILI Wireless in Car Handsfree Speakerphones, Portable Bluetooth Speaker,Stereo Sound Enhanced Bass/Built-in Mic/TF Card Player/Google Assistant Voice Command for Car, Home, Outdoor After charging this device with the supplied micro-USB cable, I tried this as a Bluetooth speaker with my LG laptop. The sound was great. I also paired it with my boyfriend's iPhone and was able to answer a call by pressing the phone image on the speaker.

It supposedly connects to up to two phones simultaneously, but I did not have another phone to try it with. Also, there is a hands-free option but in order to use it, one would have to be playing music via a Bluetooth enabled in car device at the time a call was coming through or via the micro SD card. The rest of the time, when a call comes in, the phone button has to be pressed. This means it is not entirely hands free.

I did find that no matter what device I paired it with, that each device took time to find this speaker. The first pairing was the most difficult and I had to turn Bluetooth on and off several times and press the M button to wait until it registered. It took a while, but T826 is what it comes up as.

Besides the sound this small speaker generates, I like the removable magnetic clip on the back. It is easy to attach to a sun visor. There is also a slot for a micro SD card where an MP3/WMA audio file can be played from.

Overall, this is very functional. It has a lanyard for carrying that also makes it portable. The unit has to be charged every once in a while. The reason I got this is to use it as a portable Bluetooth speaker and not for answering calls.

IN THE PACKAGE
- speaker

- micro USB charging cable
- instructions

Jabra Elite 85h Wireless Noise-Canceling Headphones, Black – Over Ear Bluetooth Headphones Compatible with iPhone and Android - Built-in Microphone, Long Battery Life - Rain and Water Resistant If you’re looking for unmatched sound reproduction in a very quiet music room, neither the Bose 35 nor the Jabra 85h is competing in that studio monitor class.

These are yeoman everyday transit use with great sound quality. It’s the noise cancelling depth that shuts out the chaos that makes the two exceptional. Ambient sustained engine/crowd noise will wear you out. That’s what makes noise cancelling central for me.

Noise cancelling – Jabra is the first headphone experience every bit the equal with the Bose 35. Other noise reduction players competing in the price bracket don’t come close. The Jabra and Bose cancellation are different. Audible net cancellation is so close to the same that I can’t discriminate. Bose noise cancelling has a sort of over-pressure feeling that I don’t notice in the Jabra. It’s not a discriminator or fatigue element either way for me. If you know what I mean, you will notice it.

Bass – Jabra by a hair

Treble – Jabra wins

Clarity – Bose by a hair

Comfort – High personal importance for air travel. Bose passes the 8-hour flight test. I believe the Jabra will too.

The Jabra 85h is incredibly impressive. It’s a competitive break-through from my perspective. The same price range as Bose 35. Overall the same with very subtle differences that make a winner impossible to my ear. I’d need an acoustics lab to compare the 2 in detail and that degree of detail would be irrelevant for me or the typical user in the price bracket.
Nobody’s going to go wrong with the Jabra 85h. Bose has the first genuine competitor in the price range. That’s good for everybody.

text_fidelity_a:
Amazon Fire HD 8 Plus tablet, HD display, 32 GB, (2020 release), our best 8" tablet for portable entertainment, Slate Update 2/9/23: My (cognitively) young son, who has that very expensive iPad mini I mentioned below in the original review, now pushes his iPad to the side at least 50% of the time and 'steals' my FirePad. There are apps and games on the FirePad that aren't on Apple's AppStore - granted, they're usually pretty basic, or else I imagine they'd be available across multiple OS platforms - but he's very young, cognitively, and he doesn't care. I am 100% certain that whenever this iPad he's got needs replacing (because Apple does that way more than is right, IMO) we will be going the 'FirePad' route.

Our family has had so many iPads, iPad Airs, iPad minis... and I can say that - when bought brand spanking new, at the time of release, we were in love. Honeymoons don't last forever, unfortunately, and neither do the tablets. NOT ONCE did we break them beyond being fixable; every single time they've 'updated out' and none of the apps worked. They're not even good for internet after awhile, because even Safari and Chrome have to be updated for use... and the updates will not work with the outdated IOS. Yknow, because $600+ for 2-4 years is acceptable. NOT. But dumb sheeple me, kept on buying them. 🤦🏼‍♀️

I bought my son a 6th Gen iPad mini last November. It was newish and on backorder til about early-mid December. I gave it to him as a gift IN A CHILDPROOF CASE. So it has been protected since I got it. Since before he got it. And two weeks ago it quit charging. Now, he uses his iPad for everything: Communication. Education. Entertainment. Besides the $600 I paid, and even with the $3.49/month AppleCare, it's just totally unacceptable. After taking it to two localish Apple Premium partners, neither of which wanted to fix it and both of which wanted to just sell me a new one, and because all our other iPads (4 that I haven't tossed yet) won't allow him to access his communication apps anymore, I cried and then ordered the Fire Mini on my 23% interest credit card because he needs accessS to something he can communicate on.

I'm, erm, a girl of a certain age. Getting more and more stubborn about learning new technology stuff. So getting used to this has been a mite frustrating for me. My son, 25 with the cognitivity and resilience of a 2 year old, hasn't skipped a beat. It's early days - and I did buy the 2 year Amazon Protection with the 'FirePad' as we call it - but for $200 plus tax, tag & title 😉 this little Fire Tablet is at least the quality equivalent of the $600 iPad Mini.

The only cons... the display IS just as good as the iPad, though the colors aren't quite as vibrant/vivid and the brightness isn't as bright. Is that worth $400 more... not for anyone I know. It just takes a little getting used to (I'm talking maybe 2 days with minimal usage by a stubborn adult) and then it's not an issue anymore. The biggest con, though, is that Google won't hop in bed with Amazon - apparently - as willingly as they do Apple. No Google app, no Chrome app, no YouTube app. I just use the Silk browser (Bing... YUCK!) type in Google for Google searches or YouTube to watch videos. Maybe 3 seconds of frustration but it does remember my YT log in after the first time, so there's that to help lessen the annoyance for when I use it. (My son watches YouTube on his TV anyway.)

CLIFF NOTES: 🔩🍎. 💸🔥
(Screw Apple. Buy Fire.)

text_fidelity_a: Bose Portable Home Speaker with Alexa Voice Control Built-in Portable Home Speaker Charging Cradle, Black This speaker has an incredible sound, particularly for its size, and is very portable which is convenient.  But it is extremely frustrating because it's so unresponsive.  Using the assistants (Google, Amazon), there is a bit of a pause before it answers or confirms what you said and then there is a long pause before it follows your instructions.  For example, if you ask it to play music, there's at least a second where you aren't sure if it heard you or not before it says it's playing that music.  Then there are a couple silent seconds before the music starts.  This has led to us attempting to ask it again, thinking it didn't "hear" us, which just confuses it.  For using during a party or something where you just start it going and leave it, it wouldn't be a problem, but for regular use, the annoyance is not worth the great speaker sound.

text_fidelity_a: Swimbuds Sport Premium Waterproof Headphones & 11 eartips in 4 Styles (Upgraded Cord) This is my second pair of Swimbuds. These swim buds are so light that they actually stay in my ear.  Short cord doesn't get tangled up.  And I guess the Christmas-tree tips are a bit different because so far these headphones are the only one that have not leaked, but I do have to insert them deep into ear canal.  I use just a touch of petroleum jelly on tips to help the insertion and to moisturise ears, because these headphones (like most other waterproof headphones) can cause irritation of the external ear canal.  There are a lot of tips to choose from.  I use them in my Endless Pool, so I don't know how they will perform in regular pool during turns and flips, but my guess is because of their lightness they will work fine.  I don't care much for clarity of music during swimming, but I found sound to be quite acceptable with these headphones.

The black range is as crisp as I have ever seen on any set. Setup is very easy and uncomplicated. The remote includes a key pad on the back to make entering information and searching easier. Again , would be a five if not for the picture going black issue.

Con: The speakers are tiny and are facing the rear . Not sure why they choose to go the cheap route and skimp on the sound. By no stretch am I an audiophile but one does notice the lack of depth to the sound and the volume level needs to be up to hear dialog clearly. A sound bar is almost a requirement and I did see that some retailers are packaging one with their Vizio TV'S to,address this concern.
The remote has a quick access buttons for Amazon , Netflix and of all things IHeart Radio. They must have got a kick back from I Heart . The quick connect feature loose a plus for choosing I Heart. Hulu or the like would have been a better choice .

I would not be afraid to buy this set. I would strongly suggest that the purchase be supported by a vendor you trust and will support the sale after the fact. Some of these are through a third party and directly through Amazon . I always select the direct Amazon route because of the support after the sale. text_fidelity_a:
Amazfit GTR 2e Smart Watch, 24 Day Battery Life, Alexa Built-in, Fitness Tracker with GPS & 90 Sports Modes, Blood Oxygen Heart Rate Tracker, 5 ATM Water Resistant, for Men Women Android iPhone,Black I'm a big fan of the Mi Band series of trackers, and this is the first device that finally got me to switch to something else. If you aren't familiar, Xiaomi and Huami aren't big brands in the US compared to other countries, but these are solid high quality products and not your standard fare Chinese junk. I've tried a LOT of different fitness trackers and smart watches- Everything from Google WearOS, Fitbit, Apple, and all the way down to the cheap trackers from Chinese throwaway brands with obscure apps. For a long time I've said I liked the features and quality of the expensive brands, but found they all had major flaws (battery life being a major one- I don't want another thing to charge as often as a phone!). The Mi band from Xiaomi was super affordable and high quality compared to others in that price range, and had a battery that only required being charged once a month.
This is basically the smarter older brother of that band. It is compatible with Mi Fit, so all my data transferred right over, but it is so much nicer than the band. For starters, the notification system is easier to read and keep up with messages, but the benefits go far beyond a larger screen. The music control is a nice touch, I like being able to pause and adjust the volume without taking my phone out of my pocket if playing on a BT speaker while I'm doing dishes, for example. The tracking is pretty accurate compared to other expensive brands, and while it doesn't support apps like Wear OS and Apple Watches, it has all the fitness functions you'd need built in already, including some fun widgets beyond the expected ones like a stopwatch, phone finder and even a compass! And unlike cheap brands, the UI is responsive and smooth. Not the smoothest out there for sure, but more than acceptably smooth considering how much a flagship smartwatch costs compared to this.
It has support for voice commands, but I honestly found that feature kind of gimmicky more than useful. The higher end version of this includes a speaker which might make the command function more useful as sort of a digital assistant, not to mention the ability to take phone calls from your wrist. But the model I got to try out lacks the speaker, which is a fine compromise for a cheaper price tag all things considered. The battery life at first was just OK, a few days on a charge if using lift-to-wake functions, but just as on my Mi Band tracker of old, I found if I turn off auto-wake and rely on using the button to wake the display, the battery life goes from counting in days to counting in weeks. That's the killer feature of this device- the ability to leave it on to track fitness and sleep habits without having to charge it so often. I'll have to charge it more than my old Mi Band's monthly top up for sure, probably at least 2x a month, but that's still very manageable.
So that's it, after years of loving my Mi Bands and considering it the standard by which all practical fitness trackers should be judged, I'm finally moving on to an Amazfit watch. This is a difficult value to beat.
text_fidelity_b: Amazfit GTR 2e Smart Watch, 24 Day Battery Life, Alexa Built-in, Fitness Tracker with GPS & 90 Sports Modes, Blood Oxygen Heart Rate Tracker, 5 ATM Water Resistant, for Men Women Android iPhone,Black

Garmin Venu Sq Music, GPS Smartwatch with Bright Touchscreen Display, Features Music and Up to 6 Days of Battery Life, Slate and Moss Green The main thing I bought this for is to monitor heart rate while hiking. Its reading is way off for me - as confirmed by a pulse ox and manually counting. The watch kept telling me my heart rate was over 100 just around the house. I have nsvt but my heart rate generally runs low. So I'm very sensitive when I have palpitations - when this watch kept saying my heart rate was over 95 I wasnt buying it. That brings into question any other readings or parameters.

I find the watch annoying and frustrating to use. The watch face does not interact very well for me. I'm constantly trying to tap it and it wont register so then the screen shuts off. Another annoying thing is it tells you to start moving around when I'm doing housework. I guess you can shut that off but I've really lost interest. Hopefully Garmin can offer some fix for the reading since its past the return date.

The positives - watch is comfortable and I don't wear jewelry. I forget its on. Its a large size so its readable if you have vision issues. I've had no problem with that.

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) My mother is having the same issue. My family all pitched in and bought her a kindle for her birthday last year and I cannot express how angry I am at the customer service and quality of this product. My mother does not have much confidence when it comes to the latest technology and was hesitant about using a tablet in the first place. However, after my family kept telling her how great it was and how much she would love it, she finally agreed to give it a try. A few months after we purchased her first kindle, it broke and Amazon sent her another one, but that kindle also broke and Amazon is refusing to replace it.

Not only has Amazon ruined her experience/impression on using tablets, but the refusal to repair the charging component so many other customers have experienced problems with is unacceptable. I am a frequent shopper of Amazon, but after hearing that my mother's second kindle is not working and Amazon has refused to replace or repair it has made me reconsider my shopping preferences. My mother no longer wants to even use the kindle, she told me not to "worry about getting it fixed" because it's been such a hassle; which is disappointing considering how much my family lobbied for the product promising her that she would love how much it would improve her life.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

text_fidelity_a: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st) Bought two of these in refurb condition and they both arrived as good as new.  After using them for a few weeks now, we both love our Kindle Fire devices and feel they are a great value for what they offer.  I still use my keyboard Kindle, loving the long battery life, and only wish the Fire could compare.  Unfortunately, even with the wi-fi turned off, this one needs a recharge much more often, but what this offers far outweighs the need to plug a cord between the device and an electrical supply.  It's easy to read, not too heavy, fits into the sleeves I'd purchased for the keyboard Kindle, and with wi-fi turned on, gives me a connection to the internet.  Love being able to use Gmail and more, don't miss having to pay more for wireless connection, do miss being to move with the device and remain connected, though.  Carousel feature is great, not having to go to archived items to identify what's in our growing library, and being able to download very easily from the icon is a time saver.  It's well worth the cost for the Kindle Fire and I recommend it to anyone who doesn't think it's a cheaper version of an iPad, expecting it to offer and provide more than its capabilities.  Two different products, each has its assets.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Fire (Previous Generation - 1st)

Ultimate Ears Boom 3 Portable Waterproof Bluetooth Speaker - Sunset Red I listen mostly to jazz in the background while I’m reading or on the web, usually at low volume - sometimes rock at louder volumes. I’ve bought any number of blue tooth speakers, as a hobby I suppose, always in search of that nirvana sound. They’ve ranged from really small Fugoo units (with unbelievably good sound) to paired floor standing auditorium behemoths that will blow your contacts out. IMO, the UE Boom 3’s are not only a good value, they are superlative in sound from low to high ranges at easy and medium volume. Great for voice, too, e.g. podcasts. I have 2 paired and will likely buy another pair (stereo is nice) for another room.

I recently tried the UE Megablast and they don’t hold a candle to to crispness and range of the Boom 3’s. They’re loud and have some nice control features but for sound, IMO the 3’s are the best by far, and uncannily the least expensive of over 10 other brands, up to $300. Unless you’re filling a large room with loud music I’d say the Boom is the best speaker in it’s portable class. Enjoy, and don’t worry about missing any sound - you’ll pleasantly hear it all!
